items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.

items.summary: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

From 3.1.0 until 4.5.1, the afpd Spotlight RPC fetchQueryResultsForContext: reply path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c calls the top-level sl_pack function from sl_pack_filemeta on a shifted sub-buffer without passing the remaining capacity of the outer DSI reply buffer. items.summary:
TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted.



 TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List<String>) builds a Typesense filter_by expression by raw string concatenation of caller-supplied document IDs into the form id: [id1,id2,...] . The Typesense id field uses bare (unquoted) values in this list form with no escaping mechanism. An ID containing characters with syntactic meaning in the Typesense filter grammar — such as a comma ( , ), a closing bracket ( ] ), or operator tokens ( || , && ) — can break out of the list literal and alter the structure of the filter expression.



 An attacker who controls a document ID passed to the delete operation can use this to delete documents other than the intended ones (comma injection), or to construct a filter that matches every document in the collection (operator breakout), resulting in unintended bulk deletion.



 Applications that pass externally supplied or user-controlled document IDs to VectorStore.delete(List<String>) backed by TypesenseVectorStore are affected.

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, sl_unpack_loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses an attacker-controlled Spotlight table-of-contents index during FPSpotlightRPC without checking it against the number of entries or the remaining dsi->commands buffer. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can choose a large toc_index whose multiplication and addition produce an out-of-range address, causing an attacker-influenced heap read and reliably crashing the worker serving that session. The earlier CVE-2026-44066 remediation bounded recursion depth and toc_offset but did not bound toc_index. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, the afpd FPSpotlightRPC unmarshalling handlers in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c trust the element count encoded in the upper 32 bits of an RPC tag without comparing it with the remaining input length. An authenticated client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can make sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_date, sl_unpack_uuid, or sl_unpack_floats iterate beyond dsi->commands and read heap memory. The read values remain in internal dalloc storage and no information-disclosure channel was demonstrated, but the worker serving the attacker's session can be crashed. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of PyTorch Foundation PyTorch. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the checkpoint format conversion utilities. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in deserialization of untrusted data. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-32834.

items.summary: Inscriptis is a Python library for converting HTML to text. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.6, when the parent is block-level, table_end_handler() in model/tag/table_tag.py writes each sibling table through HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() in model/html_element.py; Canvas.open_block() leaves the parent padding_inline prefix on the stack, Canvas.close_block() does not remove it, and only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). Each following sibling table therefore carries forward accumulated indentation, making get_text() output grow quadratically and allowing small attacker-controlled HTML to exhaust memory in applications converting it without authentication or user interaction. This issue is fixed in 2.7.6.

items.summary:
In Apache Karaf, the default command ACL configuration for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg, defined in assemblies/features/standard/src/main/feature/feature.xml and the child-instance template instance/src/main/resources/org/apache/karaf/instance/resources/etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start, and feature:stop to users with the admin role, while leaving feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove without ACL entries.


Because Karaf's command guard (SecuredSessionFactoryImpl) allows commands with no matching ACL rule (NO_MATCH) to execute, an authenticated SSH user holding only the ssh and viewer roles can execute feature:requirement-add bundle:<uri> (or feature:<name>). RequirementAdd forwards the requirement directly to FeatureService.addRequirements(), causing the resolver to download, install, and start an arbitrary bundle with the Karaf JVM process's full authority, bypassing the admin-only restrictions on feature:install and bundle:install. Similarly, feature:requirement-remove allows removing provisioning requirements and uninstalling features/bundles.

MitigationUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




For existing deployments or upgrades that preserve existing files in etc/, add the following rules to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg (and any child instance etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg files):




requirement-add = admin 

requirement-remove = admin

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

When sftpEnabled=true (the default configuration in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg), the SSH server exposes the karaf.base directory tree through the MINA SSHD SFTP subsystem and SCP command factory without verifying the authenticated user's roles beyond the initial sshRole login check. Consequently, an authenticated user with only low-privileged roles (such as viewer and ssh) can read sensitive configuration and key files (including etc/users.properties and etc/host.key) or write arbitrary bundles/configurations into monitored directories (such as deploy/ or etc/), leading to privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.


Apache Karaf 4.4.13 and 4.5.0 introduce the sftpRole configuration property in org.apache.karaf.shell (defaulting to admin) and enforce role-based access control on SFTP subsystem creation, SCP command execution, and virtual filesystem access.

Mitigation / WorkaroundUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




On earlier versions where SFTP/SCP access is not required, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart the SSH server bundle (or Karaf instance).

items.summary:
The shell command ACL for the feature scope (etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg) restricts feature:install, feature:uninstall, feature:start and feature:stop to the admin role, but had no entry for feature:requirement-add or feature:requirement-remove.

The provisioning resolver turns a requirement into the same install/start (or uninstall) action as feature:install / feature:uninstall: a bundle: requirement causes an arbitrary bundle to be downloaded and started, and a feature: requirement installs that feature. Because the two commands had no ACL, a user authenticated with only the viewer (and ssh) role could invoke them and cause Apache Karaf to download, install and start an attacker-chosen bundle, which then runs with the full authority of the Karaf process — thereby bypassing the admin-only authorization enforced on feature:install and bundle:install.

This is the same class of issue as the feature:repo-add -i / feature:repo-remove -u bypass, on sibling commands not covered by that earlier fix.Mitigation:Upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.12 or 4.5.0 (or later), which restrict feature:requirement-add and feature:requirement-remove to the admin role.

As an interim workaround on affected versions, add the following two lines to etc/org.apache.karaf.command.acl.feature.cfg; the change is picked up at runtime without a restart:

requirement-add = admin

requirement-remove = admin

items.summary:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way.

The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown.

This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.

A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

items.summary: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

items.summary:
A flaw was found in CRI-O's container-creation environment-variable handling
(`mergeEnvs` in `server/utils.go`, consumed by `setupContainerEnvironmentAndWorkdir` in
`server/container_create.go`). When a `CreateContainer` request supplies a `nil` CRI
`Envs` field, CRI-O falls back to using the target OCI image's `config.Env` entries
unfiltered, in contrast to the normal merge path, which validates each entry for a
`key=value` form before use. An OCI image whose `config.Env` contains an entry with no
`=` character (e.g. a bare `NOEQUALS` string) causes CRI-O to split that entry into a
single-element slice and then index its second element, which is out of range. This
triggers an unrecovered Go runtime panic in the `crio` daemon process, crashing it and
terminating the container-runtime service for all workloads on the node until it is
restarted.

items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

items.summary: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image (for example, via USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image) can trigger this flaw without user interaction, as libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events. This could lead to limited information disclosure or denial of service.

items.summary:
Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .

items.summary:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

items.summary: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in GStreamer's RTSP support library. The vulnerability occurs while parsing an Authorization or WWW-Authenticate header that uses Digest authentication. Specially crafted whitespace placement around a parameter's terminator can cause an internal length calculation to underflow, leading to a crash of the process parsing the header. On an RTSP server this can be triggered by a remote, unauthenticated attacker sending a single malformed request when the server has authentication enabled; the same flaw can also be triggered against an RTSP client by a malicious or compromised RTSP server. Successful exploitation results in a denial of service (application crash) and has no confirmed impact on confidentiality or integrity.

items.summary:
An algorithmic complexity flaw exists in libsoup's HTTP Range header processing that persists after the CVE-2025-32907 fix.

CVE-2025-32907 addressed memory amplification when a client repeated the same range many times in a single Range header. Commit 9bb92f7a corrected merge correctness in soup_message_headers_get_ranges_internal() in libsoup/soup-message-headers.c, but the coalescing loop still removes merged ranges using g_array_remove_index() for each coalesced element. Because GArray is contiguous, each mid-array removal performs an O(N) memmove. When many identical satisfiable ranges are supplied (for example bytes=0-0 repeated thousands of times), the loop performs O(N²) work coalescing them into a single range.

The vulnerable path is reachable server-side from handle_partial_get() in libsoup/server/http1/soup-server-message-io-http1.c when a SoupServer handler returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty body. No authentication is required. The number of ranges is bounded only by the maximum request header size (~100 KiB), allowing roughly 25,000 ranges per request. Reporter measurements on libsoup HEAD containing the CVE-2025-32907 fix show ~90 ms single-core CPU per such request at the wire maximum, blocking the server's event loop for that duration.

This is a CPU exhaustion / availability issue only. No memory corruption or information disclosure occurs.

Affected: libsoup versions containing the CVE-2025-32907 fix but not merge request !550.
Fixed upstream: MR !550 merged 2026-08-20, replacing per-element removal with O(N) in-place compaction and rejecting Range headers requesting more than 200 ranges.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/issues/538
Related: CVE-2025-32907

MCUboot's PSA-crypto ECDSA adapter parses the RFC 5480 DER signature with parse_signature_from_rfc5480_encoding() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/ecdsa.h, which takes no length argument. bootutil_ecdsa_verify() explicitly discards the signature length ((void)slen;) and the parser walks the encoding using length bytes read from the buffer itself (r_len = sig[3], then a derived s_len), with no check that those offsets stay within the supplied signature. Because this parsing runs before psa_verify_hash(), a malformed signature triggers the read whether or not the signature is valid.

In bootutil_img_validate() (boot/bootutil/src/image_validate.c:404) the ECDSA signature TLV is gated only by len > sizeof(buf), since EXPECTED_SIG_LEN() is the constant 1 for ECDSA; len is attacker-controlled in the range 0..128 and is copied into the 128-byte stack buffer buf. With a crafted r_len (e.g. sig[3] = 255) the parser's memcpy reads roughly 130+ bytes past the end of buf, an out-of-bounds read of adjacent stack memory. Reaching the signature case only requires a key TLV that matches a trusted public key (public material), so the path is effectively pre-authentication.

The defect is gated to the PSA crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_PSA_CRYPTO) with MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC256/MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384 (and MCUBOOT_SIGN_EC384 always builds with PSA); the in-tree CC310, TinyCrypt, and mbedTLS adapters use different decoders and are not affected. This is not a signature bypass: the over-read bytes feed a verification that fails closed and are never returned to the attacker, so there is no information leak. The impact is bounded to a possible fault/denial-of-service on memory layouts where the read crosses an unmapped region; on typical flat-memory MCUs it reads adjacent RAM without faulting.
This vulnerability was reported independently twice: by NVIDIA Project Vanessa on 2026-06-22, and by Kai Phan (@kaimandalic) on 2026-07-19 as GHSA-r44p-8v6p-hqv4, which is closed as a duplicate of this advisory. Both original reports are reproduced in full below. The second report additionally observes that bootutil_ecdsa_parse_public_key() discards its end pointer ((void)end;, ecdsa.h:446). That observation is correct, but it is not part of this vulnerability and is not counted in the severity: the buffer it parses is bootutil_keys[key_id].key, the compiled-in trusted key store (image_ecdsa.c:54-55), so no attacker-controlled data reaches that parse. It is a robustness gap on the same code path and should be closed alongside the signature-parser fix. Note also that the second report's proof-of-concept models the signature buffer as an 8-byte heap allocation and therefore reports a heap overflow; in MCUboot the buffer is the 128-byte stack array buf, gated by len > sizeof(buf), so the real over-read is of adjacent stack memory.

items.summary:
MCUboot's Espressif port omits zeroization of two sensitive stack buffers in boot/espressif/hal/src/flash_encrypt.c. In check_and_generate_encryption_keys(), the freshly generated XTS-AES flash-encryption key is held in the stack array keys[BLOCKS_NEEDED][32] (flash_encrypt.c:216), written to eFuse via esp_efuse_write_keys(), and the function returns (flash_encrypt.c:243) without scrubbing it. In esp_flash_encrypt_region(), the plaintext flash sector buffer buf (flash_encrypt.c:454) retains the last sector's cleartext at both the success and flash_failed returns. Neither path performs a memset/bzero/mbedtls_platform_zeroize, even though the same port already does bzero for key digests in boot/espressif/hal/src/secure_boot.c.

The affected code runs only on the Espressif port with CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, and only during the one-time first-boot provisioning pass when flash encryption is not yet enabled (boot/espressif/main.c); on subsequent boots the buffers are never created. Recovering the residue requires an out-of-band stack/RAM-disclosure primitive — JTAG/debug halt, UART ROM download, a core/crash dump, or a warm-boot RAM scrape — captured during that single provisioning boot. Under the recommended CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_RELEASE plus secure boot, those channels are fused off and no exposure exists.

The practical impact is a low-severity, defense-in-depth hardening gap: a flash-encryption key (and last plaintext sector) may linger in bootloader stack memory. Because the eFuse key block is burned read+write-protected, the transient stack copy is the only readable copy, and only during one boot; in a development build where a disclosure channel is open, an attacker with that capability can usually already read the still-plaintext flash directly, so the marginal confidentiality gain is small. Confirming real-world recovery depends on a specific SoC/debug configuration not exercisable from source alone.

items.summary:
The Cypress/PSoC6 flash-map backend in boot/cypress/cy_flash_pal/cy_flash_map.c guards every flash access with assert() against the wrong struct field. flash_area_read(), flash_area_write(), and flash_area_erase() check assert(off < fa->fa_off) and assert(off + len < fa->fa_off), comparing the area-relative off against the partition's absolute base address fa->fa_off instead of its length fa->fa_size. Because fa_off is a large absolute address, realistic out-of-partition offsets pass the check even in a debug build, and under NDEBUG the asserts are removed entirely. The access then proceeds as memcpy() (or a flash row op) at fa->fa_off + off with no enforcement.

The MCUboot core does not bound image-region offsets itself; it relies on flash_area_read() returning an error. During pre-authentication image validation, bootutil_img_hash() in boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_img_hash.c loops over ih_hdr_size + ih_img_size + ih_protect_tlv_size — all attacker-controlled header fields of the still-unverified update image — calling flash_area_read(), and the TLV iterator in boot/bootutil/src/tlv.c reads attacker-derived offsets the same way. An attacker who can stage a crafted image in the secondary/update slot (via OTA, DFU, or serial recovery, depending on the product) declares an oversized ih_img_size, causing reads far past the partition. A correct backend would reject these and fail validation cleanly; the Cypress backend does not.

The out-of-bounds access is in the source address of the copy — the destination buffer is correctly sized — so there is no memory corruption, no information disclosure to the attacker (the data is only folded into a hash that still fails the signature check), and no authentication bypass. The realistic impact is a bus fault or hang when the computed absolute address lands on an unmapped or peripheral region of the PSoC6 address map: the bootloader crashes instead of rejecting the bad image, an availability (denial-of-service) impact. The defect is specific to the Cypress/PSoC6 port; mainline Zephyr/sim/mynewt backends are unaffected. The identical broken guard in the write/erase primitives is a latent out-of-bounds-write gap, but no attacker-controlled out-of-bounds offset was found to reach those (serial-recovery uploads are bounded by the core), so the reachable memory-safety bug is the out-of-bounds read.

items.summary:
When MCUboot resumes an interrupted image swap it takes the number of bytes to move straight from the flash-resident status trailer. In boot_swap_image() (boot/bootutil/src/loader.c) the fresh-swap branch recomputes copy_size from the image headers and is bounded — swap_run() in boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c carries an explicit "not enough free space" check (last_idx >= first_trailer_idx) — but that check runs only inside if (boot_status_is_reset(bs)). On the resume branch the code instead does boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); copy_size = bs->swap_size; and passes the value to swap_run() with no re-derivation and no bound.

swap_run() turns that byte count into a sector index by summing sector sizes until it reaches the count, with no ceiling on the real sector count: find_last_idx() in swap_move.c and swap_offset.c, and find_last_sector_idx() in swap_scratch.c, are all while (1) loops. The resulting index is fed to boot_img_sector_off() / boot_img_sector_size() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_priv.h), which index the fixed BOOT_MAX_IMG_SECTORS sectors[] arrays with no bounds check. Past num_sectors the loop reads zero-initialised — and past BOOT_MAX_IMG_SECTORS, adjacent-struct — entries; a sector size of 0 makes the loop never terminate, and a bogus computed offset is handed to boot_erase_region() / boot_copy_region() as an out-of-bounds flash erase or copy.

MCUboot itself only ever writes a validated, slot-bounded swap_size (swap_misc.c, fixup_revert()), so reaching the defect requires writing the trailer from outside. Serial recovery provides exactly that: an upload writes attacker bytes contiguously from offset 0 of the primary slot (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c, via flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot()), bounded only by img_size <= area_size, so it controls the whole trailer — magic, swap_info, op/idx/state and swap_size. The resume gate boot_status_is_reset() keys solely on those op/idx/state fields, and boot_find_status() explicitly trusts valid magic as implying valid metadata. A forged in-progress status with an oversized swap_size therefore drives the unbounded walk during swap setup — before the primary image's signature is validated, and serial recovery is unauthenticated by design.

The outcome is an out-of-bounds flash erase or copy, or a non-terminating loop, inside the bootloader: an unbootable or bricked device, with the possibility of bootloader memory corruption. That exceeds what serial recovery is designed to grant, which is only the ability to stage an image that must still pass signature verification.

Exposure requires a swap-based update backend — MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_MOVE (the default for swap builds), MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_SCRATCH or MCUBOOT_SWAP_USING_OFFSET; overwrite-only, direct-XIP and RAM-load builds are unaffected — together with MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY. Without serial recovery the path is only reachable by an attacker who can already write flash directly, which is outside the threat model.

The fix is to treat the trailer's swap_size as untrusted: reject or clamp it in boot_swap_image() before it becomes copy_size, bounding it by the primary slot's usable image area (sector count x sector size, excluding the trailer) rather than the raw flash_area_get_size(), and aborting recovery with a non-zero error on overflow. The same guard should cover the independent boot_read_swap_size() reads in each backend's boot_read_image_header().

items.summary:
The vendored zcbor decoder's zcbor_any_skip() in boot/zcbor/src/zcbor_decode.c descends one C-stack frame per level of CBOR nesting. On a list or map it copies the decoder state (memcpy(&state_copy, state, sizeof(zcbor_state_t))) and recurses once per member, with no depth cap: the skip path does not use zcbor's backup stack, and ZCBOR_MAX_ELEM_COUNT is SIZE_MAX, so nothing bounds how deep the recursion goes.

That function is reached on attacker-controlled bytes before any authentication. MCUboot's serial-recovery command parser decodes SMP/CBOR requests with zcbor_map_decode_bulk() (boot/boot_serial/src/zcbor_bulk.c), which skips any map key it does not recognise by calling zcbor_any_skip() on the encoded value; the echo handler in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c calls it directly on the same footing. Both run during image upload, long before the uploaded image's signature is checked. The default receive buffer is MCUBOOT_SERIAL_MAX_RECEIVE_SIZE = 512 bytes and each nesting level costs a single byte to encode (0x81), so roughly 500 levels of nesting fit in one request — comfortably more than a bootloader's stack can absorb, since every frame carries a full zcbor_state_t copy plus locals.

The impact is availability only: the bootloader's stack overflows and the device faults or hangs during recovery. There is no controlled out-of-bounds write that escapes the DFU buffer, no disclosure, and no authentication bypass — the recursion grows the stack with the decoder's own internal state. Whether a given board actually exhausts its stack depends on that board's bootloader stack size, which we did not measure; the fix is nevertheless unconditional, because an unauthenticated pre-authentication code path must not have its safety depend on a per-board stack margin.

Exposure requires MCUBOOT_SERIAL (serial/SMP recovery), which is not enabled by default, and recovery entry is normally gated on a physical pin (CONFIG_BOOT_SERIAL_ENTRANCE_GPIO / PIN_RESET), with a no-valid-image fallback path. Products that expose serial recovery over an externally reachable transport, or that fall into recovery when no valid image is present, are the ones at risk.

The fix is to bound the skip: thread a recursion-depth counter through zcbor_any_skip() (or have zcbor_map_decode_bulk() reject values nested beyond a small constant) and fail once the limit is exceeded — equivalently, take the bounded-skip implementation from upstream zcbor.

items.summary: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.15 through 0.10.0, the value of a host-scoped credential header was exposed to other hosts via HTTP redirects. SendAuthenticatedWebRequestBlock attaches a host-scoped credential's headers to a request, but once a redirect took that request to a different origin, only three fixed header names (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie) were removed. A host-scoped credential's header names are free-form (the UI suggests X-API-Key), so a credential carried under any other name followed the redirect to the new origin. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

DNSSEC support is not compiled in by default and must also be enabled at runtime.

A remote attacker can open idle TCP connections to port 53 and occupy the entire pool, preventing new TCP DNS connections and DNSSEC validation that requires TCP fallback. UDP DNS resolution continues, and occupied slots are released after a fixed lifetime.

In PXE network-boot environments this can substitute attacker-chosen boot content for a victim machine.

items.summary: A flaw was found in jwcrypto. The JWK.import_key() function validates the key_ops JWK member for duplicate values using an algorithm with O(n^2) time complexity, and the length of key_ops is not bounded. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can supply a JWK with a large key_ops array to an application that passes attacker-controlled key material to a public key-import API (reachable via ECDH-ES key agreement, OIDC dynamic client registration, DPoP, or ACME account key registration, among others) to consume excessive CPU time, resulting in a denial of service.

items.summary: A flaw was found in the ChunkReader component of the Undertow web server, which is used to handle chunked transfer encoding in HTTP requests. The issue occurs because a security check for the chunk size is performed before the value is shifted, allowing a specifically crafted 15-digit chunk size to bypass the limit and overflow into internal state flags. This can cause the server to terminate a request body prematurely and interpret the remaining data as a separate, smuggled request.

items.summary: A flaw was found in GNOME Shell. A malicious or compromised remote search provider could exploit this by providing oversized icon dimensions, leading to an out-of-bounds read. This can cause the GNOME Shell process to crash, disrupting the user's session, and potentially disclose sensitive information from adjacent memory.

This could lead to unauthorized changes in file ownership and permissions on arbitrary files, potentially compromising system integrity and availability by altering system or application states or rendering services unusable.

items.summary: A flaw was found in libtpms, a library that provides software TPM 2.0 emulation. When restoring TPM 2.0 state (for example during a virtual machine's power-on or state/migration restore), a malformed state blob can supply an oversized skip-block length that is not validated against the remaining size of the input buffer. This can drive an internal size counter negative, which bypasses a subsequent bounds check due to an unsafe signed-to-unsigned conversion, causing the parser to read memory outside the bounds of the heap buffer holding the state data. Successful exploitation can crash the process hosting libtpms (such as swtpm), resulting in a denial of service of the emulated TPM device and the virtual machine that depends on it. No data corruption or information disclosure was confirmed.

items.summary:
Summary

MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds.

This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites.

Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation

In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0):

boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success).
boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0.
boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend.

Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status.

Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability).

Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer

boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure.

Reachable-security sites (center the fix here)

1. boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:193 — inconsistent-status assert(0), falls through to complete swap. A2 + !VALIDATE_PRIMARY. [worst]
2. boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:278 — same, swap-offset backend.
3. boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:239 — same, swap-scratch backend.
4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL.

(Truncated. The full description is in the advisory: https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/security/advisories/GHSA-cr9j-p626-pwcc)

items.summary:
MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer.

The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption.

A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size.

Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144).

On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.

items.summary:
Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

A user with valid credentials for an expired account can exploit this flaw to bypass access controls and authenticate to the system. This allows unauthorized access to persist after the account was intended to be deactivated.

A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the Kerberos Credential Manager (KCM) responder during Kerberos ticket-granting ticket (TGT) renewal, where a deferred callback accesses memory that has already been released. An authenticated local user with a renewable Kerberos ticket can trigger this issue on systems configured with KCM renewal, causing the KCM responder service to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

items.summary: A flaw was found in SSSD. An issue in the Kerberos Credential Manager (KCM) responder allows a local user to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by maintaining a persistent connection and repeatedly storing and destroying credentials. Because the service fails to release cached objects from memory when credentials are removed, memory consumption grows continuously, ultimately exhausting available memory and rendering the service unresponsive.

A remote attacker who can reach an affected transport interface can send a specially crafted compressed request and obtain data from outside their own request. Exploitation of the exposed remote-cluster transport interface does not require authentication.

items.summary: A flaw was found in sblim-cmpi-base. Insecure temporary file creation in the provider registration scripts allows a local unprivileged user to perform a symlink attack. By creating a symlink in a world-writable directory, an attacker can redirect privileged writes to an arbitrary file during script execution in a privileged context. This can lead to the overwrite of root-owned files, potentially disrupting system services or operation. Exploitation is conditional on the script running with elevated privileges and may be mitigated by sticky-directory symlink protections.

items.summary: A flaw was found in libefiboot, a component of efivar. The device path node parser in libefiboot fails to validate that each node's Length field is at least 4 bytes, which is the minimum size for an EFI (Extensible Firmware Interface) device path node header. A local user could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted device path node. This can lead to infinite recursion, causing stack exhaustion and a process crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

items.summary: A flaw was found in the file-icns plugin in GIMP. When applying a decompressed mask during ICNS image processing, the plugin reads from the mask data buffer without verifying if the cursor exceeds the allocated resource size. If a crafted file contains a truncated mask resource, the icns_decompress function continues reading past the bounds of the buffer. This out-of-bounds read vulnerability results in information disclosure of heap contents, where memory contents are leaked as alpha channel pixel values, or a crash leading to a denial of service if unmapped memory is accessed.

items.summary: A flaw was found in the file-sgi plugin in GIMP. When processing an RLE-compressed SGI image, the plugin allocates memory for a row table. The image header dimensions (ysize and zsize) are read as 16-bit unsigned integers. If a crafted file sets both dimensions to their maximum value (65535), the multiplication ysize * zsize overflows the standard 32-bit int boundary before being passed to calloc. This integer overflow issue results in undefined behavior, aborting the plugin and causing a denial of service.

This occurs when multiplying num_colors and num_cluts, both 16-bit unsigned short integers, resulting in a value exceeding the maximum integer limit. An attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted image file, leading to undefined behavior and causing the GIMP plug-in to abort, effectively resulting in a denial of service.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of pass_through_endpoints. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of code before it is executed via module import. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-31433.

An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

items.summary: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.10.0, a user can add a version under another user's workflow ID and take over its Marketplace listing. An attacker with an account and the target's workflow ID can replace the creator's pending Marketplace submission with their own, so that approval installs the attacker's workflow under the creator's listing. Without reviewer involvement, the attacker can also stop the owner from saving new versions and break runs that name no version. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

items.summary: A vulnerability in the GRUB2 bootloader has been identified in the normal module. This flaw, a memory Use After Free issue, occurs because the normal_exit command is not properly unregistered when its related module is unloaded. An attacker can exploit this condition by invoking the command after the module has been removed, causing the system to improperly access a previously freed memory location. This leads to a system crash or possible impacts in data confidentiality and integrity.

items.summary: A vulnerability has been identified in the GRUB2 bootloader's normal command that poses an immediate Denial of Service (DoS) risk. This flaw is a Use-after-Free issue, caused because the normal command is not properly unregistered when the module is unloaded. An attacker who can execute this command can force the system to access memory locations that are no longer valid. Successful exploitation leads directly to system instability, which can result in a complete crash and halt system availability. Impact on the data integrity and confidentiality is also not discarded.

items.summary: A vulnerability has been identified in the GRUB (Grand Unified Bootloader) component. This flaw occurs because the bootloader mishandles string conversion when reading information from a USB device, allowing an attacker to exploit inconsistent length values. A local attacker can connect a maliciously configured USB device during the boot sequence to trigger this issue. A successful exploitation may lead GRUB to crash, leading to a Denial of Service. Data corruption may be also possible, although given the complexity of the exploit the impact is most likely limited.

BusyBox ftpd Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Read and Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information on affected installations of BusyBox. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ftpd service, which listens on TCP port 21 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create or delete files or disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-27555.

items.summary:
DeepSpeed _get_zero_stage Deserialization of Untrusted Data Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of DeepSpeed. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of checkpoint data. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in deserialization of untrusted data. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-29242.

KDE Gwenview PNG File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of KDE Gwenview. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of PNG files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-29373.

Opening an attacker-controlled HDF5 file and reading an affected metadata attribute can execute attacker-controlled code in the consumer’s process. No fixed version is available as of this review.

items.summary: browser-use before 1.0.0 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability in the SecurityWatchdog's _is_url_match function that allows attackers to bypass domain restrictions by exploiting a raw-string startswith() comparison instead of parsed hostname validation. Attackers can craft URLs using userinfo injection or domain prefix confusion (e.g..com@attacker.com or .com.attacker.com) to redirect an LLM-controlled navigation to an arbitrary host, exfiltrating sensitive data such as secrets embedded in the URL to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

items.summary: browser-use before 1.0.0 contains a URL parser differential vulnerability in SecurityWatchdog that allows attackers to bypass allowed_domains, prohibited_domains, and block_ip_addresses checks by crafting a URL with a backslash before the allowed host, exploiting the mismatch between urllib.parse hostname extraction and Chromium's WHATWG-style URL parsing. Attackers can influence an LLM-controlled navigate action, such as through prompt injection, to send requests to loopback or private addresses or arbitrary external hosts before the browser redirects to about:blank, enabling SSRF and persistent state changes on the target server.

items.summary: A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

items.summary: Allot's Subscriber Management Platform (SMP) v18.3.53 stores sensitive configuration credentials protected by a product‑wide, hard‑coded master password. The master key is constructed using a hard-coded string value plus a default key value. This results in an effective encryption key that is recoverable from shipped scripts and configuration files. The platform uses a deprecated and cryptographically insecure algorithm (PBEWithMD5AndDES) and no documented mechanism exists to change the key. An attacker with read access to configuration files, backups, or diagnostic bundles can recover credentials and TLS keystore/truststore passwords, and access to subscriber-management operations and subscriber PII.

items.summary: Lookyloo is a web-based URL capture and analysis platform. Prior to the fix, the authorization mechanism for private captures (seed-based access control) was not consistently enforced at the data access layer. The capture_cache method and numerous internal methods (get_info, get_meta, get_statistics, get_modules_responses, get_data, get_video, get_screenshot, get_har, get_cookies, get_storage_state, get_frames, get_console_messages, get_capture, get_ressource, misp_export, lacus_export, ai_export, comparator functions, and others) could be invoked with only a capture UUID without validating the required seed token. This meant that API endpoints and internal code paths that called these methods directly could return private capture data to unauthenticated users or users lacking the correct seed. The before_request hook in the web interface provided a partial check, but the underlying data layer did not enforce it, creating an inconsistent authorization boundary. An attacker who knew or guessed a private capture UUID could potentially access sensitive data including rendered screenshots, HAR files, downloaded files, cookies, storage state, console messages, and MISP exports through various REST API endpoints and web routes. The fix introduces a LookylooPrivateCapture exception raised at the cache layer when a private capture is accessed without a valid seed, refactors the API to pass CaptureCache objects (already validated) rather than raw UUIDs, and ensures all web and API endpoints propagate the session-known seed or admin status to the data access layer. Background processes use an explicit unsafe=True flag to bypass the check, as they operate server-side with full trust.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a listener performing DTLS 1.2 resumption accepted a session created by an outbound client connection without checking which role created it. A malicious server previously contacted by the application can retain the outbound session secret, select the client-side cached session through its session key, and present it to the application's reachable listener when both connections share a SessionStore. The attacker must first complete an outbound connection. WebRTC users are not affected. The listener can accept application data without running its normal PSK callback or client-certificate authentication checks, allowing a peer trusted only for an outbound connection to gain unauthorized listener access. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

Upgrading the agent in place does not replace the shared key, and deleting the agent's Vault breaks instances managed through Default Host Management Configuration.

items.summary:
An out-of-bounds write issue exists in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple calls into the minimum documented output buffer. A remote user who supplies crafted ciphertext might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. Affected are all versions of AWS-LC before 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x before 4.2.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x before 3.6.0, and AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x before 2.0.18.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS-LC 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.2.0, or AWS-LC-FIPS 3.6.0.



AWS-LC-FIPS 2.0.18 is also fixed; AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x reaches end of support in April 2027.

A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover.

On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

items.summary: A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

An attacker with access to these logs can obtain credentials for the customer's external storage. The issue affects deployments with ES|QL federation enabled and audit logging configured to record the affected request information.

items.summary: The Live Composer – Free WordPress Website Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.2 via deserialization of untrusted input in the dslc_module_posts_output shortcode. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 1.2.2 until 3.1.13, the server state machine did not distinguish successful processing of the client certificate flight from completion of the handshake, so later traffic could revisit the same cached Certificate, ClientKeyExchange, and CertificateVerify messages. A malicious client can withhold Finished and send additional handshake traffic. Depending on the configured authentication policy, repeated work can include certificate parsing, handshake signature verification, and certificate-chain verification. The vulnerable endpoint must act as the DTLS server. Pion WebRTC applications are affected when they operate in that role. Repeated or concurrent attempts can consume excessive CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.4 until 3.1.13, the handshake cache copied and retained submitted messages without deduplicating entries, limiting the entry count, limiting total payload bytes, or stopping new insertions after handshake completion. A remote peer able to deliver suitable DTLS traffic can grow the cache through incoming handshake messages and repeated caching of outgoing retransmissions for the lifetime of the connection. The fragment reassembly buffer's separate size limit does not prevent this issue because completed messages are retained in the append-only handshake cache. Unbounded cache growth can exhaust application memory and cause a denial of service. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.0.0 until 3.1.13, peer certificates were parsed and their RSA public keys were passed to handshake signature and certificate-chain verification without an explicit modulus-size limit. A remote peer can provide a certificate with an unusually large attacker-chosen RSA modulus and an invalid signature; no corresponding private key or valid handshake signature is required to trigger the expensive operation. An RSA verification path must execute. A local ECDSA certificate does not prevent the peer from presenting an RSA certificate, and WebRTC deployments can be affected. Repeated or concurrent malicious handshakes can consume substantial CPU resources, delay legitimate connections, and reduce service availability. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a server with a SessionStore saved the session ID and master secret after ClientKeyExchange, before receiving a valid Finished message and before enforcing the configured client-authentication checks. A remote client can omit its Certificate message, send ClientKeyExchange, leave the first handshake unfinished, and then resume the cached session using the master secret it learned during key exchange. The server must use a SessionStore and negotiate a certificate-based cipher suite. The attack can bypass client certificates required through RequireAnyClientCert or RequireAndVerifyClientCert, or a rejecting VerifyConnection callback. WebRTC users are not affected. The abbreviated handshake can allow unauthorized access to application data. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

items.summary: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.0.0 until 3.1.13, the implementation selected signature verification based on the certificate public key while deriving the digest from the peer-controlled signature scheme without validating that the scheme, key type, and hash requirements were consistent. The affected verification functions are verifyKeySignature for ServerKeyExchange and verifyCertificateVerify for CertificateVerify. An unauthenticated network attacker who can redirect a DTLS handshake and obtain the genuine peer certificate can submit crafted handshake signatures that are accepted without possession of the certificate private key. This can let the attacker impersonate the peer and compromise the confidentiality and integrity of protected traffic; checking a WebRTC SDP certificate fingerprint does not prevent the attack because the genuine certificate is presented. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.13.

items.summary:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or inject SQL through a forged keyset pagination cursor.

Ash.Page.Keyset.filter/4 in lib/ash/page/keyset.ex decodes the client-supplied page[:after] or page[:before] cursor from Erlang external term format and rejects decoded expressions with Ash.Expr.expr?/1. That check does not examine the fields of a struct. The cast of each value against the type of its sort field accepts structs for the :ci_string, :map, :struct and :term types. A struct in the cursor value for such a sort field therefore reaches the data layer. With AshPostgres, the read passes such a struct to inspect/1, which runs the Inspect implementation of the struct module that the attacker selected. A chain of struct modules from ecto and db_connection then calls a function that the cursor names, which permits OS command execution. An %Ash.Query.Function.Fragment{} inside an %Ash.CiString{} value is written into the SQL query as raw text.

This issue affects ash: from 3.31.3 before 3.38.0.

items.summary:
Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_ses (ExAws.SES module) allows path injection into Amazon SES V2 request URLs.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/ses.ex and program routines ExAws.SES.delete_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.get_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.update_contact_list/2, ExAws.SES.create_contact/3, ExAws.SES.get_contact/2, ExAws.SES.update_contact/3, ExAws.SES.delete_contact/2 and ExAws.SES.list_contacts/1.

The V2 contact-list and contact functions interpolate the caller-supplied list_name into the request path without URI-encoding it, unlike the email address in the same functions which is passed through ExAws.Request.Url.uri_encode/1. An application that forwards untrusted input as a contact-list name lets an attacker embed /, .. or ? to escape the intended contact-lists/<name> path segment. A value such as x/../suppression/addresses/victim%40example.com makes a delete_contact_list/1 call arrive at the account-wide suppression list. The request is still signed with the application's own AWS credentials and sent to the configured SES host, so the impact is cross-resource request forgery inside the caller's own AWS account, not arbitrary SSRF. Applications that only use hardcoded or strictly validated list names are not affected.

This issue affects ex_aws_ses: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.0.

items.summary:
ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes.

Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.summary:
ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-separated list without escaping. Grantee email and id values are wrapped in double quotes and joined with a comma, but double-quote, comma, and CR/LF characters in the value are not neutralized. An application that passes an attacker-influenced grantee value (for example an email address taken from a "share this object" feature) into an ACL grant option (grant_read, grant_write, grant_read_acp, grant_write_acp, or grant_full_control) lets the attacker close the quoted token and inject an additional grantee, such as the attacker's own canonical id or the predefined AllUsers group URI, into the header. S3 then applies the injected grantee, granting an arbitrary principal the same permission (up to full control or public access) in an unintended ACL grantee-injection and privilege-escalation issue.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.summary:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key.

ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the x-amz-copy-source request header by interpolating the source bucket and object key directly into "/#{src_bucket}/#{src_object}" with no percent-encoding. The sibling function put_object_copy percent-encodes the bucket and each path segment before assembling the same header, but upload_part_copy skips encoding entirely.

When the source key is derived from untrusted input, reserved characters (spaces, ?, &, =) pass through verbatim and corrupt the copy-source reference, so the copy targets the wrong object or fails. A key containing \r or \n can split or inject additional headers into the outgoing HTTP request, depending on how the configured HTTP backend serializes headers.

Applications that pass a source bucket or object key derived from untrusted input to ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 are affected. Applications that only ever pass trusted, well-formed keys are not affected.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to make presigned URLs and presigned POST forms point at a host of their choice.

With virtual_host: true, s3_accelerate: true or bucket_as_host: true, ExAws.S3.presigned_url/5 and ExAws.S3.presigned_post/4 build the URL from the bucket name without checking it. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com..., and the signature is computed for that host. Clients given the URL upload their files to, or download content from, the attacker's host, and every such URL discloses the access key id. With bucket_as_host: true any valid hostname works as the bucket name.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.summary:
XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via unescaped, caller-supplied values.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/s3.ex and program routines ExAws.S3.put_bucket_logging/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_notification/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_replication/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_website/2.

The bucket-configuration body builders construct their XML by interpolating caller-supplied values directly into the request body without escaping, and never route them through the module's own escape_xml_string/1 helper. A value containing XML metacharacters (<, >, &, quotes) can close the intended element early and open attacker-chosen elements, which the builder's trailing closing tag then closes, keeping the document single-rooted and well-formed. In a multi-tenant application where tenants configure their own bucket settings, an attacker who can influence one of the interpolated field values (for example the logging target, a notification ARN, a replication destination or Account, or a website redirect HostName) can inject arbitrary configuration nodes into a request the application signs and sends to AWS. The affected builders are reached through the public functions put_bucket_logging/2, put_bucket_notification/2, put_bucket_replication/2, and put_bucket_website/2.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.5.9 before 2.6.0.
